topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, student cohorts, and key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Biological basis of cancer in genetic changes and tissue architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer develops through accumulated genetic alterations that disrupt normal cellular differentiation and three-dimensional tissue architecture.

topics.label: Tumour invasion, metastasis, and histological progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate the clinical and histological characteristics of tumour invasion, routes of metastasis, and the stepwise progression from benign lesions to invasive malignancies.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature and clinical behavior of benign growths
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the formal naming conventions for tumours and explain how benign growths behave and present clinical risks.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer mortality and patterns of incidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how tumour growth causes systemic illness and death, alongside the patterns of tumour incidence in human populations and across multicellular species.

topics.label: Clinical presentation and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the clinical signs of tumour development and evaluate the diagnostic approaches and effectiveness of population screening programmes.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a review of learning objectives and reminders regarding upcoming practical sessions.
